Show the hand starting at mark 3 and moving forward by exactly two positions to land on mark 5, explicitly labeling this first destination as 'Mark 5'.

A visual demonstration showing that the '+2' rule applies to any starting number, not just zero. Specifically, show a hand starting at mark 1, jumping forward two positions (past 1 and 2) to land on mark 3, reinforcing that the movement is relative to the current position.

Show the cumulative distance traveled as a number line or stack of blocks: 7 jumps of size 2 equals a total length of 14. Then show that on a circle of size 7, a length of 14 fits exactly twice (14 = 2 * 7), meaning you complete two full loops and land precisely back at the starting point.
